title: Article 71 — Matters relating to, or connected with, the election of a President or Vice-President

content.overview: Article 71 provides that all doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a President or Vice-President shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court, whose decision shall be final. Parliament may by law regulate any matter relating to or connected with the election (including the grounds on which such election may be questioned). The election is not to be called in question on the ground of any vacancy of the electoral college. If the election is declared void, acts done by the person in exercise of Presidential or Vice-Presidential powers before the date of the decision are not invalidated.
content.glance: Election disputes of President/VP: exclusive SC jurisdiction; decision final. Parliament may regulate. Vacancy in electoral college no ground. Acts before voiding decision protected.
content.study:
Article 71:
(1) Doubts and disputes relating to election of President or Vice-President → Supreme Court; decision final.
(2) Parliament may by law regulate matters relating to such election (including grounds of challenge).
(3) Election not open to challenge on the ground of any vacancy among the members of the electoral college.
(4) If election declared void, acts done before the date of the decision in the exercise and performance of Presidential/VP powers and duties are not invalidated by reason of that declaration.

Examination: exclusive SC forum; finality; parliamentary regulation; vacancy-no-ground rule; protection of past acts.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Election disputes: Supreme Court only; decision final.
2. Parliament may regulate election-related matters by law.
3. Vacancy in electoral college is not a ground to question the election.
4. Acts done before a voiding decision remain valid.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Where are disputes relating to the election of the President or Vice-President decided?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 71, all doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a President or Vice-President are inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final. Parliament may by law regulate matters relating to such elections. The election cannot be questioned on the ground of any vacancy in the electoral college. If the election is declared void, acts done by the person as President or Vice-President before the date of the decision are not invalidated.

examTips: SC exclusive; final; vacancy no ground; past acts protected.

keyTakeaways: Art 71: President/VP election disputes — SC exclusive and final.
